reasoning_traces.think:
Each NFL offensive scheme defines a geometric and temporal framework for route execution. The West Coast Offense optimizes for short, high-frequency horizontal passes within a bounded time window, mapping to a compact route tree with minimal vertical threat. Air Coryell maximizes vertical stretch through deep routes, requiring sustained pass protection and arm strength—its efficacy depends on the spatial separation of defenders and the quarterback's ability to deliver under pressure. Air Raid emphasizes tempo and personnel density, leveraging a high-pass frequency to exploit mismatches in coverage depth and defender positioning. Erhardt-Perkins abstracts play calling into conceptual identifiers, enabling rapid adaptation but demanding high cognitive processing from players. These primitives form a dual structure: one rooted in spatial route geometry and temporal constraints, the other in semantic abstraction and mental computation. Each scheme's failure mode reflects a breakdown in either physical execution (e.g., pass rush, coverage jamming) or cognitive alignment (e.g., miscommunication, coverage confusion).
